Keep all section headings below. -->

#### References to other Issues or PRs
See https://github.com/sympy/sympy/issues/31086#issuecomment-6891811101

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed
Before `Ordinal` could accept values in non-canonical ordering.
```
>>> from sympy.sets.ordinals import *
>>> Ordinal(OmegaPower(0,3), OmegaPower(0,2))
3 + 2
>>> Ordinal(OmegaPower(0,3), OmegaPower(0,2)) + 1
3 + 3
```
Now it raises `ValueError`.

#### Other comments
In the longer term, it may be better to for the `Ordinal` constructor to do the canonicalization itself.

#### AI Generation Disclosure
NO AI USE

#### Release Notes


<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* sets
  * ordinals: fixed a bug where `Ordinal` could produce non-canonical outputs.
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->
diff:
diff --git a/sympy/sets/ordinals.py b/sympy/sets/ordinals.py
index 23780846e26a..da8006f35958 100644
--- a/sympy/sets/ordinals.py
+++ b/sympy/sets/ordinals.py
@@ -87,7 +87,7 @@ def __new__(cls, *terms: OmegaPower):
 
         obj = super().__new__(cls, *terms)
         powers = [i.exp for i in obj.args]
-        if not all(powers[i] >= powers[i+1] for i in range(len(powers) - 1)):
+        if not all(powers[i] > powers[i+1] for i in range(len(powers) - 1)):
             raise ValueError("powers must be in decreasing order")
         return obj
 
diff --git a/sympy/sets/tests/test_ordinals.py b/sympy/sets/tests/test_ordinals.py
index d87e3e7af824..2ebf485b8990 100644
--- a/sympy/sets/tests/test_ordinals.py
+++ b/sympy/sets/tests/test_ordinals.py
@@ -72,3 +72,7 @@ def test_atomic_classes():
 
 def test_ordinal():
     assert Ordinal() is ord0
+
+def test_ordinal_canonical():
+    assert raises(ValueError, lambda: Ordinal(OmegaPower(0, 3), OmegaPower(0, 2)))
+    assert raises(ValueError, lambda: Ordinal(OmegaPower(0, 1), OmegaPower(1, 1)))

linked.author: MajesticSlacks
linked.body:
This has come up a few times now, most recently in https://github.com/sympy/sympy/pull/29733#discussion_r3178471780.
```
>>> from sympy import *
>>> from sympy.sets.ordinals import *
>>> S.Zero == ord0
False
>>> 0 == ord0
True
>>> S.Zero == 0
True
>>> sin(ord0)
AttributeError: 'OrdinalZero' object has no attribute 'as_coefficient'
>>> sin(0)
0
>>> sin(S.Zero)
0
>>> 
```
In the sense of SymPy, it seems to me that finite ordinals and `int`s could be considered unequal, in that they don't support the same operations.
linked.title: Should finite `Ordinal`s evaluate as equal to `int`s and `Integer`s?

title: sets: Fixed a bug where `Ordinal` can produce non-canonical output.
